title: FiO2 versus PaO2 with high shunt
subtitle: Response of arterial oxygenation to inspired oxygen fraction in severe true shunt

patient.summary: A 58-year-old mechanically ventilated patient with severe multifocal pneumonia and dense alveolar consolidation refractory to moderate oxygen levels.

prediction.question: When FiO2 is increased from 0.40 to 1.00 in this patient with extensive alveolar filling (45% shunt), how do PaO2, SpO2, and PaCO2 respond?

whatToLookAtHint: Compare the magnitude of change in PaO2 and SpO2 against what would normally be expected from a large increase in inspired oxygen, and check PaCO2.

reflection.question: Why does delivering 100% inspired oxygen produce only a modest increase in arterial PaO2 in this patient?

options.text: True right-to-left shunt bypasses ventilated alveoli entirely; because capillary blood from ventilated units is already nearly 100% saturated, dissolved oxygen cannot overcome the mixing of severely desaturated shunted blood.
FiO2 1.0 causes instantaneous total absorption atelectasis, reducing diffusing capacity to zero.
Hyperoxia stimulates diffuse precapillary vasoconstriction, shutting down pulmonary blood flow completely.
Oxygen molecules displace carbon dioxide from hemoglobin, preventing further oxygen binding by allosteric inhibition.

reflection.explanation: True shunt (Qs/Qt = 0.45) represents blood traversing unventilated, fluid-filled alveoli. Even though PAO2 rises from ~239 to ~670 mmHg in ventilated units, end-capillary hemoglobin is already on the flat portion of the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve. The only additional oxygen carried by ventilated blood is dissolved O2 (0.003 mL/dL per mmHg PO2). When this mixes with 45% desaturated mixed venous blood, PaO2 increases only modestly (from ~45 to ~55 mmHg), demonstrating classic shunt refractoriness.

evidence.claim: True shunt is refractory to oxygen therapy because capillary blood in ventilated units is already fully saturated and cannot carry enough extra dissolved oxygen to compensate for venous admixture.
evidence.source: West JB, Luks AM. West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials. 10th ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2016:63-78.

evidence.claim: In patients with severe shunt fractions exceeding 30%, increasing FiO2 to 1.0 yields only minimal increments in PaO2 without PEEP recruitment.
evidence.source: Petersson J, Glenny RW. Gas exchange and ventilation-perfusion relationships in the lung. Eur Respir J 2014; 44(4):1023-1041.
